title: Run job checks on GitHub CI via athena/ci/<job id> branch, with local
summary: Wire the existing ci_result::resolve and routing::run_routed into the job run. Push the admitted candidate to athena/ci/<job id>, wait up to a configured bound for CI on that exact SHA, and use green or red results. Fall back to local checks otherwise, pass verify::reuse_statement to the verifier, and delete the branch at close. The goal is to cut local build time and disk use; the audience is the Athena maintainer.

defaults_applied.how: All changes are Rust plus config and workflow files.
Criteria require new tests plus clippy and fmt clean.
Behavior criteria run cargo test, clippy and fmt.
The wait bound is configuration in athena.toml and the SHA rule is enforced in code.
Criteria check local checks not running and the branch pushed and deleted, not wiring existence.
The outcome is no local check run on a green exact-SHA CI result.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs (run_routed call near line 1265, where check_runs is produced), crates/athena-core/src/routing.rs (run_routed, CiSource stub with no push yet), crates/athena-core/src/ci_result.rs (resolve, Wait, Source, CiRecord), crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs (reuse_statement), crates/athena-core/src/gh/client.rs (GhClient implements CiSource), crates/athena-data/src/config.rs (athena.toml config structs), crates/athena-git/src/lib.rs (git operations). Order: admission, then push of the CI branch, then the checks stage resolves CI, then the verifier. No new record or data file is added, so the records validation allow-list (check_record_file, AnyRecord) is not touched. Source is measured directly through the injected fakes counting local check invocations.
The wait bound is a new key in athena.toml with a default of 25 minutes (1500 s), read through crates/athena-data/src/config.rs.
Branch deletion runs on every close path (accepted, rejected, failed) and a deletion failure is logged, not fatal.
Push failure, no remote, or no GitHub configured means the local checks run as today.
The exact name of the git push and delete methods is chosen by the producer from crates/athena-git/src/lib.rs, adding them if missing, behind an injectable trait for tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: cargo test passes, including a new test in crates/athena-core where the injected CI source returns a green result for the candidate's exact SHA: the local check runner is called zero times and the check records name CI as the source.

cargo test includes new tests showing a red CI result fails the job with the failing check's name in the reason and no local run, a result for a different SHA is ignored and the local checks run, and a missing, cancelled or timed-out result falls back to the local checks.
cargo test includes a test where the injected git and platform sources record that athena/ci/<job id> is pushed after admission and deleted at close, for accepted and for failed outcomes.
cargo test includes a test showing that with no remote or no GitHub configured, no push happens and the checks run locally.
The verifier prompt input built in crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs includes the text from verify::reuse_statement when the check record's source is CI (Grep for the call).
athena.toml has a CI wait bound key set to 25 minutes, and the config struct in crates/athena-data/src/config.rs parses it.
.github/workflows/ci.yml triggers on push to branches matching athena/ci/** (Grep the on: block).
cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test all pass.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing CI-backed checks, and docs/design/ci-routing.md section 10 items 4 and 5 are updated from Not done.

out_of_scope: Changing what the CI workflow checks beyond its trigger.
Giving the producer access to GitHub, or running real network calls in tests.
Changing the local check implementation or the SHA rules in ci_result.rs beyond what wiring needs.
departures: Larger than the typical job: it touches the run pipeline, config, git and workflow files, so cost, time and failure risk are higher.
urgent_reason: Cuts the 15 to 18 minute local check time per job and the low-disk failures that waste whole attempts.
hard_reason: Changes the run pipeline's checks stage and its pass/fail gate, so a mistake could wrongly accept or reject candidates.
